solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Alive to the scope of relief

parts.note: a living creature is still breathing
scope means room, space to operate

explanation.surface: Someone alive to how much comfort a remedy can bring.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or respite from pressure is a welcome relief, time to recover before carrying on.

clue.text: Gaudy town like Hollywood?

definitions.meaning: showy and cheaply glittering, like Christmas decorations
Hollywood's nickname joins this glittery word to 'town', so the question mark asks for the first half of that nickname

explanation.surface: Is a showbiz town like Hollywood merely gaudy?
explanation.definitionFit: Glittery strands of decoration are the byword for showy cheapness, and they name Hollywood's nickname.

clue.text: Posthaste

parts.note: split in two, the word gives 'post' (send off) and 'haste' (speed), both meanings of one word

explanation.definitionFit: Sending something off and doing it with great speed are both senses of the same word, as in 'with all despatch'.

clue.text: Payments cause dissent; rubs me up the wrong way

indicators.note: rubbing someone up the wrong way upsets them, and these letters are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: Paying out money causes arguments and irritates the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid out from a fund is recorded as outgoings, a formal word for payments.

clue.text: Short time to change ends at the dance

indicators.note: the last two letters of the word for a short time swap places at its end

parts.note: a minute is a short space of time

explanation.surface: A brief moment to swap sides at the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately triple-time ballroom dance of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

clue.text: Art lover makes haste to have summer in Paris

indicators.note: the word haste is made into something else, its letters rearranged

parts.note: été is French for summer

explanation.surface: An art enthusiast rushes to spend the summer in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to beauty and the arts is an aesthete, a refined lover of art.

clue.text: Stopped racket by French queen

indicators.note: the noise sits by the queen, coming after her in the answer

parts.note: reine is French for queen
a racket is a din, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A noisy disturbance near a French queen was halted.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse is to pull it up, so the phrase means checked or stopped.

clue.text: Find out we get income support included at college

indicators.note: the benefit abbreviation is included within the word we

parts.note: IS is the abbreviation for Income Support, a British state benefit
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Students discover that benefits are counted while at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To become aware of the truth, wake up to it, is to find it out.

clue.text: Vocal support for the male wangling his place upstairs

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so a word that sounds like a support is wanted

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or building

indicators.note: wangling means fiddling or manipulating, so these letters are fiddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A spoken prop helps a man manoeuvre his way into a better home upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstairs' is the upper house of Parliament, the House of Lords, where hereditary nobles sat.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble entitled to sit in the House of Lords, the upper chamber, has his place upstairs.

clue.text: Praying to find another junior mastermind

indicators.note: another arrangement of these letters is required

explanation.surface: A prayer for a second clever child.
explanation.definitionFit: A child with extraordinary talent is a young genius, a junior mastermind.

clue.text: Author may propose alternative group backing

indicators.note: backing means the letters are read backwards
a group of letters sits inside the words propose alternative

explanation.surface: A writer might suggest another set of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist credited with fables such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Somewhere to sit for lots of food and endless drink

parts.note: a banquet is a lavish feast

indicators.note: the word for the drink loses its final letter

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A feast and unlimited drinks make a fine evening out.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholstered bench along a wall, as in a restaurant, is a place to sit.

clue.text: Cover composer's hesitation

parts.note: Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A stand-in musician hides the composer's reluctance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun case worn at the hip or shoulder is a protective cover for a pistol.

clue.text: Style suited to cedar

indicators.note: suited means adapted or fitted, so these letters are refitted

explanation.surface: A design fashion that suits cedarwood furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s is a design style.

clue.text: Opponents past having one repeat direction

parts.note: in bridge, North and West sit as opposing players
by means past, as in 'walk by'
one of the two opponents named is given again

explanation.surface: Rivals going by, with one repeating the path.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North partners South and West partners East, so North and West are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point between north-west and west is a direction.

clue.text: He interviewed Jenkins without difficulty at first

indicators.note: without means outside, so the politician's first name goes around the rest

parts.note: Roy Jenkins, British Labour politician and Chancellor
a bind is an awkward difficulty

indicators.note: only the first letter of at is used

explanation.surface: A broadcaster quizzed the politician Jenkins with ease at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Robin Day was a famously combative BBC political interviewer who questioned figures like Roy Jenkins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Robin Day was a famous British television political interviewer.

clue.text: Most immature guy set on mayhem

indicators.note: mayhem is chaos, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The most childish fellow sets out to cause havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: The least grown-up, lowest in age, is the most immature.

clue.text: Magnificent birds returned carrying one pound

annotationWithheld.why: Magnificent birds returned carrying one pound (7): the only parse is EMUS containing I+LB, the whole reversed (EMILBUS backwards), with 'returned' standing between the pieces it turns; the reversal-split rule refuses a whole reversal over a container and no single-piece reversal gives SUBLIME
annotationWithheld.clue: Magnificent birds returned carrying one pound

clue.text: Completely at home with Dorothy's dog

parts.note: in means at home
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Fully settled in with the dog from Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means as a whole, entirely, completely.

clue.text: Chef got fat, so they say, on meat dish

indicators.note: so they say means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: Roux is a famous family of chefs (Albert and Michel Roux) and lard is fat, said together in non-rhotic British speech

explanation.surface: Gossip says the cook put on weight from eating meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled slice of meat wrapped around a filling is a classic meat dish.

clue.text: Walker is better without a top on

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a better is removed

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: A hiker is better off with no top on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strolling at a leisurely pace is a walker.

clue.text: Girl has nothing but rubbish, journalist explained

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
O is nought
tat is cheap rubbish
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A young woman has only junk, the reporter explained.
explanation.definitionFit: A text with explanatory notes added has been explained, glossed by comments.

clue.text: Part of house starts to buckle in bad weather

indicators.note: the first letter goes in the stormy weather word

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind, bad weather

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of buckle

explanation.surface: A section of a home begins to give way in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular top of an end wall under a pitched roof is part of a house.

clue.text: Orders film's to be put back in can? No, the reverse!

indicators.note: in signals one piece going inside another
the exclamation flips the containment, so the can goes into the film rather than the other way

parts.note: ET, Spielberg's film, with its possessive s

indicators.note: put back means the word can is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ordering a movie reel to be stored in its tin, or rather the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to decree or make law, so it means orders.

clue.text: Barrier that keeps soldiers at bay?

definitions.text: Barrier that keeps soldiers at bay?

parts.words: Barrier that keeps soldiers at bay?
parts.note: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg, and until the top is cracked off the hard casing keeps them out

explanation.surface: A military defence holding back troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers here are the British breakfast toast fingers dipped into a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer casing of an egg stops toast fingers reaching the yolk inside.
